title: Nature: publishing group, ownership and control
summary: Nature is a British scientific journal published through Nature Portfolio, part of Springer Nature. The latest financial disclosure reviewed reports Holtzbrinck interests of 50.6% and a BC-backed shareholder interest of 32.1% at 30 June 2026. A July 2026 clearance for Holtzbrinck to acquire sole control creates uncertainty about subsequent governance changes.

edges.description: The journal's publisher is identified as Nature Portfolio.
Nature Portfolio belongs to Springer Nature. This describes the portfolio's group affiliation rather than a quantified equity interest in a separately verified company.
The half-year report attributes 50.6% to Holtzbrinck. This is an indirect group interest: the annual report identifies GvH Vermögensverwaltungsgesellschaft XXXIII mbH as the direct shareholder.

gaps: UKSG's opened report, https://www.uksg.org/newsletter/uksg-enews-613/holtzbrinck-can-take-over-springer-nature/, reproduces the Bundeskartellamt's 7 July 2026 clearance for Holtzbrinck to acquire sole control. Clearance does not establish completion. No completed transaction or revised ownership percentages were verified, so sole control is not asserted as a current edge.

The 2025 annual report describes pooled voting and nomination rights shared by GvH33 and Galileo Participation. Because the July 2026 transaction could change these arrangements, their continued operation is unresolved and they are not presented as current control edges.

The investor-relations shareholder chart was opened but its individual slices were not exposed in the accessible text. Other shareholders and any treasury holdings have not been quantified; no aggregate remainder is inferred.

Nature's official journal-information and portfolio-about pages failed to open. The publishing-brand relationship therefore relies on the opened Wikipedia article. Nature's opened legal notice identifies Springer Nature Limited as the website legal entity, which alone does not establish ownership of the journal.
The graph follows the publishing-brand route within three relationship levels. It does not reproduce the separate UK corporate chain found in Companies House or every intermediate holding company.
The subject is the British journal Nature, not the entire Nature Portfolio or similarly named magazines. No Wikidata identifiers were verified.
